text:
maria: FYI — after the rolling kernel 5.15.68 upgrade in ap-southeast1 a bunch of P4 nodes failed provisioning for multi-node jobs this morning. Autoscaler started falling back to smaller instances and we hit NCCL handshake timeouts on training queues.

devon: seeing the same. Pods get scheduled but MPI jobs fail during peer connect. Logs show repeated "nccl: p2p connect failed" and a flurry of nvidia probe deferred messages.

sasha: can you paste the dmesg lines? is it the DKMS symbols or a driver/ABI mismatch?

maria: here's the snippet from one host:```
[  12.345678] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  12.346000] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[  12.346200] nvidia 0000:00:1f.0: Unknown symbol nvidia_uvm_vma_map (err 0)
[  12.346500] nvidia: probe of 0000:00:1f.0 failed with error -22
[  12.346800] nv-host: dma map failed, fallback to CPU copy
```

li: that Unknown symbol line looks like kABI mismatch — DKMS didn't rebuild for 5.15.68 on those images. We've got an image-builder job that skipped kernels with new CONFIG changes.

jay: confirmed at scale — ~12% of P4 fleet in ap-southeast1 landed on the new kernel without a proper DKMS nv driver, so nvidia modules deferred. MPI jobs time out because NCCL falls back to IB and then p2p fails.

maria: ops-bot triggered a redeploy of the image-builder but we need a short-term mitigation because customers are queued. Any safe runtime workarounds?

devon: we can temporary taint the nodes and force scheduling off them: `kubectl taint nodes <pattern> gpu-kernel-unstable:NoSchedule` — quick but disruptive. Also could set a nodeAffinity to prefer eu-west2 where inventory is healthy.

oncall: tagging @oncall for capacity plan and quicker rollback option.

ops-bot: [system] kernel-rolling-update started in ap-southeast1 at 2048001000 by infra-deploy. Current status: 60% complete, 14 hosts failed module load.

li: alternative workaround: load a backwards-compatible NV driver build manually until DKMS completes. Steps we used:```
sudo apt-get install build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)
sudo dkms install -m nvidia -v 525.85 --kernelsourcedir=/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
sudo modprobe nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
```
But that requires sudo access and is messy at scale.

jay: could also set the kernel-boot param `nvidia.NVreg_RegistryDwords=Version=525`? not ideal.

maria: ops, what's the cost impact if we move queued jobs to eu-west2 on-demand instead of waiting for fixes? Rough estimate?

oncall: moving ~20 large training jobs to eu-west2 on-demand adds ~35% hourly cost due to reserved capacity shortage + egress. Estimated $2.6k/day incremental if we keep them on until image-builder finishes.

devon: cheaper path: isolate problematic nodes, spin up a small temporary Dedicated pool in ap-southeast1 with pinned kernel/image (pre-upgrade), and drain workloads away from the corrupted nodes. That uses reserved commit if available, otherwise it's on-demand but smaller surface area.

li: I can build a minimal AMI with kernel 5.15.67 + verified DKMS against our NV drivers and push into ap-southeast1. ETA ~90m if we prioritize.

maria: please prioritize. Also let's block further kernel rollout until we validate DKMS success. ops-bot, can you pause the rollout?

ops-bot: [system] rollback request queued. Pausing rollout for ap-southeast1.

sasha: after AMI builds, add a post-upgrade check to fail the rollout if `modprobe nvidia` or `nvidia-smi` return errors. Proposed check:```
if ! nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 1; fi
```

jay: Agreed — and add an automated smoke test for NCCL: launch a 2-node allreduce job and expect success within 30s. If it times out, mark the hosts as bad and roll back.

maria: I've opened a customer incident and notified teams. Devon, Li, Sasha — coordinate the AMI build and smoke test. I'll inform support and the growth team about capacity gating and possible SLA implications.

li: starting AMI build now. tagging this thread with `#priority` and `#kernel-upgrade` for tracking.

devon: I'll prepare a kubectl one-liner to taint and drain the stuck nodes after we identify them:```
kubectl get nodes -l hw-type=p4 -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl taint node {} gpu-kernel-unstable:NoSchedule --overwrite && kubectl drain {} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

oncall: if AMI build slips beyond 2h we escalate to rolling rollback of kernel package and revert to pre-upgrade snapshots. That will be more disruptive but restores service.

maria: thanks — keep updates here. I'll post when support tickets indicate customer impact thresholds hit. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(20 messages total)
